title: Deviation in a Small-Angle Prism
notes: **Small-angle approximation:** when the prism angle $A$ is small and angles are in radians, $\sin\theta \approx \theta$.
**Approximate deviation:** $\delta \approx (n - 1)A$. The deviation depends only on the refractive index and the prism angle, not on the angle of incidence.
**Why it simplifies:** for thin prisms used in spectrometers and binoculars, this formula gives sufficient accuracy without solving the full prism formula.
**Dispersion from thin prism:** $\delta_v - \delta_r = (n_v - n_r)A$. The angular separation between violet and red is proportional to the prism angle and the dispersion of the material.
**Practical consequence:** a thinner prism gives less deviation and less dispersion, which is why high-precision instruments use carefully chosen prism angles.
